Volume values $v$ are linearly remapped from a per-field mapping range $[R_{min}, R_{max}]$ into $v' \in [0, 1]$ using $v' = \frac{v - R_{min}}{R_{max} - R_{min}}$ [S1].

The evidence explicitly states under the 'Range' parameter description: 'Each field can have its own mapping range. The volume will be linearly remapped from this range into the 0..1 range.' While the evidence does not provide the specific mathematical formula $v' = (v - R_{min}) / (R_{max} - R_{min})$, the claim describes the standard linear remapping process defined by the text ('linearly remapped... into 0..1'). In the context of technical documentation verification, the textual description of the operation supports the claim of how the values are treated, and the formula provided in the claim is the correct mathematical definition of the described linear remapping. Therefore, the facts in the claim are consistent with and supported by the evidence.

*   **Mode:** Controls ramp usage. 'No Ramp' uses values unclamped and unaffected. 'Clamped Ramp' clamps values to 0..1 before applying the ramp. 'Periodic Ramp' takes the modulus of values with 1 before sending to the ramp, useful for checkerboard or striped effects [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the description of the 'Mode' parameter found in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states: 'Mode Controls the use of the ramp. If set to No Ramp, the volume’s values are used unclamped and unaffected by the ramp. Clamped Ramp will clamp the volume’s values to the 0..1 range and then apply the ramp. Periodic Ramp will take the modulus of the volume’s values with 1 and send that to the ramp, which can be useful to create checkerboard or striped effect...'
